raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`vllm bench forward` defaulted `max_num_batched_tokens` to at least 8192 even when no case used a prefix-cache hit. The engine uses that value as the memory-profiling batch, so small decode/verify-only case sets profiled a much larger batch than they run, which can make KV-cache planning fail at high `--gpu-memory-utilization`.

This derives the default from the cases while keeping an explicit `--max-num-batched-tokens` unchanged.

## Claims

- The default budget is now the largest case's query tokens plus draft tokens plus 1024 tokens per prefix-cache hit, with `1` for an empty case list.
- An explicit `--max-num-batched-tokens` still wins.
- A six-case decode/verify set that previously profiled 8192 tokens now profiles 792 instead of 432/792 query tokens plus drafts.

## Validation

### Duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for `max_num_batched_tokens forward`, `bench forward 8192`, `forward benchmark batched tokens`, and `max_num_batched_tokens in:title`. No open PR changes the default in `vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py`.

Related but different work found during the search:

- #62139 changes the global `SchedulerConfig` default for multimodal/ASR runs.
- #60900 decouples DeepEP dispatch size from `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- #64608 changes the Whisper default.
- #62939 and #54046 describe DSpark adaptive-verification token budgets.

None of these touch the `vllm bench forward` default.

### Reproducer and tests

Added tests to `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py` covering per-case derivation, the six-case decode/verify set, explicit-value precedence, and the empty case list.

On the base code (tests only, same `_make_engine_args` path as current main):

```text
$ pytest -q tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k "derives_batched_tokens or keeps_explicit_batched_tokens"
5 failed, 1 passed
# assert 8192 == 32
# assert 8192 == 792
# ... (prefill and prefix-hit cases also assert 8192)

$ pytest -q tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k "positive_budget_without_cases"
1 failed  # assert 8192 == 1
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest -q tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k "forward_derives or forward_keeps_explicit"
7 passed
```

### Before/after

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `--case decode=32*1@8192` | 8192 | 32 |
| `--case verify=16*6@4096:5` | 8192 | 176 |
| six decode/verify cases | 8192 | 792 |
| explicit `--max-num-batched-tokens 1234` | 1234 | 1234 |
| no cases (with `--max-num-seqs 1`) | 8192 | 1 |

### Lint

`pre-commit run --files ...` passed all applicable hooks (ruff check/format, typos, markdownlint, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and the remaining repository checks). `git diff --check` is clean.

### Environment note

Local unit tests ran on CPU with an existing CPU virtual environment because a fresh `uv pip install -e .` stalled while downloading from PyPI. The full test file in that environment reached 17 passed and 8 skipped; `test_bench_forward` needs a `vllm` CLI executable and GPU, and `test_balanced_routing_restores_expert_bias` needs the missing `orjson` package. Upstream CI runs the canonical environment.

## Details

### Root cause

`_make_engine_args` applied `max(8192, ...)` when `--max-num-batched-tokens` was unset. `max_num_batched_tokens` sizes the memory-profiling dummy batch (`profile_run -> _dummy_run(self.max_num_tokens, is_profile=True)`). A six-case decode/verify set with 432 query tokens and 360 draft tokens therefore profiled 8192 tokens instead of 432/792, increasing non-KV memory. At high `gpu_memory_utilization`, the KV budget can then go negative and startup fails with `No available memory for the cache blocks`.

### Behavior and tradeoffs

- The 1024-per-prefix-hit term preserves the existing bounded-replay approximation. A model whose replay window is larger than 1024 tokens may still need an explicit budget.
- Draft tokens are counted conservatively: verify queries already include them, so the derived value can be slightly larger than the executed batch. The error is in the safe direction and far below the old floor.
- There is no behavior change when the flag is explicit, and no change to the scheduler or model runner.

### AI assistance

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to prepare this change. The human submitter must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.

**Draft:** this PR is a draft awaiting human submitter review; it is not ready to merge.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

</details>

CI triage: both failures are base-only and unrelated to this PR.

- `pre-commit` fails on `main` at `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:1214` (`F811` / mypy `no-redef` for `process_weights_after_loading`, first defined at line 1207). Tracked by #65081 and fixed by #65080.
- The Read the Docs build reports 6 `mkdocs_autorefs` warnings, all from the unchanged `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/mono/kernels/attn_frag.py` (lines 27 and 635): https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35572281/. No open PR or issue currently tracks these docs warnings.

This PR only changes `docs/cli/README.md`, `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py`, and `vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py`. The targeted pre-commit run on those files and DCO pass. Keeping this as a draft and will rebase/re-run after #65080 lands; the docs check still needs a separate main fix.

files.patch:
@@ -138,6 +138,8 @@ vllm bench {forward, latency, serve, throughput}
 
 Benchmark the model forward of exact batches: each case lists its requests as `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` (query length Q, KV length K including the query, D draft tokens). A prefill's prefix is a prefix-cache hit unless `c` marks a chunked prefill; they differ only on models with SWA bounded replay, which recompute the last window of a hit. Each request's prefix length varies by ±50% by default (`--kv-len-jitter`), identically on every DP rank. Each forward is captured as a one-shot CUDA graph; target sampling, rejection sampling, and CPU overhead aren't measured. Use `torchrun`, one process per GPU, for DP/TP/EP/PCP/PP. CUDA only for now. Add `--profile-dir DIR` to write a Perfetto trace and a per-kernel GPU time summary of each case; `python -m vllm.benchmarks.forward.profile A.kernels.json [B.kernels.json]` prints a summary or compares two. Under Nsight Systems, `nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-range-end=repeat --cuda-graph-trace=node` records just those replays, one report per case.
 
+Without `--max-num-batched-tokens`, the benchmark derives the budget from the cases: the largest case's query and draft tokens plus 1024 tokens per prefix-cache hit. Pass the flag to set it explicitly. The derived value sizes memory profiling and the runner's buffers, so it avoids profiling a batch much larger than the benchmark actually runs.
+
 ```bash
 vllm bench forward \
     --model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \

+def _forward_engine_args(*argv):
+    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser()

+    return _make_engine_args(args, [parse_case(c) for c in args.case])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("case", "expected"),
+    [
+        ("prefill=4096", 4096),
+        ("hit=2048@10240", 3072),

+        ("verify=16*6@4096:5", 176),
+    ],
+)
+def test_forward_derives_batched_tokens_from_case(case, expected):
+    """Default budget covers query, draft and prefix-replay tokens of a case."""
+    assert _forward_engine_args("--case", case).max_num_batched_tokens == expected
+
+
+def test_forward_derives_batched_tokens_for_decode_verify_set():
+    """A 432-query-token set with 360 draft tokens needs 792, not the 8192 floor."""
+    cases = [
+        "decode4k=72*1@4096",
+        "verify4k=72*6@4096:5",
+        "decode16k=48*1@16384",
+        "verify16k=48*6@16384:5",
+        "decode32k=24*1@32768",
+        "verify32k=24*6@32768:5",
+    ]
+    argv = [item for case in cases for item in ("--case", case)]
+    assert _forward_engine_args(*argv).max_num_batched_tokens == 792
+
+
+def test_forward_keeps_explicit_batched_tokens():
+    """An explicit user budget wins over the derived one."""
+    engine_args = _forward_engine_args(
+        "--max-num-batched-tokens", "1234", "--case", "verify=16*6@4096:5"
+    )
+    assert engine_args.max_num_batched_tokens == 1234
+
+
+def test_forward_derives_positive_budget_without_cases():
+    """An empty case list still yields a legal positive budget."""
+    assert _forward_engine_args("--max-num-seqs", "1").max_num_batched_tokens == 1
+
